summary: Reproduced deterministic corruption when RunAI-marked reusable-buffer views were retained by the NVFP4 online MoE loader, then cloned only marked tensors at the three pending-storage sites: FP8 weights, FP8 scales, and gated w1/w3 weights. Added routed-expert, shared-expert, scale-first, gated-pair, and unmarked-tensor coverage.

tests.what_was_measured: Before the source fix, the synthetic reusable staging buffer deterministically overwrote all three retained RunAI-marked tensor cases; 3 tests failed and the unmarked boundary test passed. Raw output: reports/j-b64a0a9c43ea/failing-before.txt

After the fix and formatting, 11 focused and neighboring unit tests passed, including routed expert weight-first, scale-first, shared expert, gated w1/w3, and unmarked reference-semantics cases. Raw output: reports/j-b64a0a9c43ea/final-tests.txt
All repository pre-commit checks applicable to the changed Python files passed. Raw output: reports/j-b64a0a9c43ea/pre-commit-after-format.txt

Confirmed the assigned device is one AMD Instinct MI350X with gfx950. This was environment evidence only; the reported reusable RunAI staging-buffer lifetime defect occurs on CPU-hosted streamed views and does not require GPU execution. Raw output: reports/j-b64a0a9c43ea/gpu-environment.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: The assigned single gfx950 GPU was detected, but no GPU kernel was used as evidence for this host-buffer ownership defect. The production NVFP4 workload described by the issue targets a different hardware/backend stack and no FP8-MoE checkpoint or distributed RunAI deployment was available.

remaining_limitations: No full FP8 MoE checkpoint was available, so full-model semantic output was not evaluated.
No distributed Kubernetes/RunAI Model Streamer deployment or tensor-parallel size 8 environment was available.
The assigned gfx950 device cannot qualify the production NVIDIA NVFP4 execution backend; validation is limited to the reported loader ownership contract with deterministic reusable-buffer views.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
